situation.problem_text:
Topic: The Fundamental Bridge: The Relationship Between Integrals and Derivatives

Target audience: University students (Calculus I)

Section: section_1 — Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy

Lecture lines:
Imagine a robot running on a straight path.
The speedometer shows its instantaneous velocity at each moment.
The total distance covered is the accumulated velocity.
Area under the speed curve equals total distance.
Distance and velocity are linked by these operations.

Planned animations:
Draw a car moving along a path (color: #FFD700) to show velocity.
Display position as the integral of velocity over time.
Use a tracer (color: #00BFFF) to mark distance accumulated.

Section: section_2 — Prerequisite Review: Graphical Slope vs. Area

Lecture lines:
Recall the derivative represents the slope of the tangent.
The integral represents the area under the curve.
Both describe the same geometric function from different perspectives.

Planned animations:
Show a line graph with a tangent (color: #FF4500).
Display a shaded region under the curve (color: #32CD32).
Morph the slope indicator into the area integrator.

Section: section_3 — The Core Mechanism: The Fundamental Theorem of Calculus

Lecture lines:
Integration is the reverse process of differentiation.
Define the accumulation function as the area under curve.
The rate of area growth equals the function height.
This relationship forms the Fundamental Theorem of Calculus.
This bridge connects local change to total accumulation.

Planned animations:
Show f(x) and its primitive F(x) side-by-side.
Draw a vertical line (color: #FFFFFF) representing the interval [a, b].
Animate the evaluation: F(b) minus F(a).
Display the integral symbol (color: #FFD700) equating to F(b)-F(a).
Highlight the equality connecting the two sides.

Section: section_4 — Visual Synthesis: Inverse Operations

Lecture lines:
Think of differentiation and integration as inverse machines.
Derivatives map a function to its rate of change.
Integration maps the rate back to the original function.
Constant C accounts for the starting point's ambiguity.
These operations perfectly cancel each other out.

Planned animations:
Represent differentiation as 'unwrapping' a curve.
Represent integration as 'rebuilding' the area.
Show both operations toggling back and forth (color: #FF00FF).

Section: section_5 — Summary & Application Check

Lecture lines:
Derivatives measure the rate of change.
Integrals measure the total accumulation.
These inverse operations underpin all of modern science.

Planned animations:
Summarize the core connection with a Venn diagram.
Apply the concept to a simple physics velocity-time graph.
Highlight the final formula (color: #FFFF00) for student takeaway.

Integration and differentiation link these concepts.

Display a [Asset: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/speedometer.svg] showing value v(t) in real time.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Intuitive Hook: The Velocity-Position Analogy", [
            "Imagine a robot running on a straight path.",
            "The speedometer shows its instantaneous velocity at each moment.",
            "The total distance covered is the accumulated velocity.",
            "Area under the speed curve equals total distance.",
            "Distance and velocity are linked by these operations."
        ])
        
        # Mobjects
        robot = Dot(color="#FFD700", radius=0.15)
        path = Line(start=self.grid["D2"], end=self.grid["D6"], color=WHITE)
        speed_graph = Axes(
            x_range=[0, 4, 1], y_range=[0, 3, 1],
            axis_config={"include_numbers": False}
        ).scale(0.3)
        velocity_label = MathTex("v(t)", color="#FFD700").scale(0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(path, "D4")
        self.place_at_grid(robot, "D2")
        self.play(Create(path), FadeIn(robot))
        self.play(robot.animate.move_to(self.grid["D6"]), run_time=2)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(speed_graph, "B3")
        self.place_at_grid(velocity_label, "A3")
        self.play(Create(speed_graph), FadeIn(velocity_label))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#00BFFF")
        tracer = Dot(color="#00BFFF", radius=0.1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject
